page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB per core, and includes a bundled 2880 GB NVMe SSD local storage volume. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, falls in the average range. However, memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck; both small-block and large-block read-only memory bandwidth benchmarks rank in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are weak, placing in the bottom 25% of tested systems.

Given the high local NVMe SSD capacity and generous memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server is well-suited for workloads requiring substantial local scratch space or caching, such as data processing pipelines, local file systems, or memory-heavy applications that do not demand high memory read bandwidth. The strong single-threaded performance supports tasks like text processing, while the weak multi-threaded decompression and database operation benchmarks suggest it is less optimal for high-concurrency transactional databases or intensive software compilation.
